businessRules.rationale: Enables incremental re-index and stable cross-run references
businessRules.rule: Stable content-addressed ids: symbol/edge ids derive from content hashes (blake3) so re-indexing is deterministic and incremental

businessRules.rationale: Avoid single-file bottleneck; support large repos
businessRules.rule: Sharded storage: soul edges/nodes partitioned by shard key so the graph scales beyond one file

businessRules.rationale: Deterministic staged transformation from source to graph
businessRules.rule: Indexing is a pipeline: extract → resolve → link → store, orchestrated by indexRepo

businessRules.rationale: Keeps query latency/cost predictable; LLM graph is precomputed
businessRules.rule: MCP server is 100% deterministic; LLM layer is authored out-of-band via enrich work-queue and overlaid, never invoked at query time

errorBehavior: Unresolved call sites recorded as gaps (gaps tool) rather than crashing index
Truncated source bodies flagged via truncated=true so analyses avoid over-claiming
invariants: Id determinism: same content → same id
Edge endpoints always resolve to real soul nodes or local LLM ids (server drops unresolved)
postconditions: After index: soul graph reflects current source at head
analysis.purpose: knowledge-crib is a deterministic code-knowledge graph system: it parses source (multi-language tree-sitter + hand-written lexers), links symbols across files into a sharded soul graph, exposes it through a CLI and an MCP server (verbs like context/impact/query/dossier), and overlays an LLM-authored semantic graph (this layer) plus a viz UI. The repo is a pnpm monorepo (TypeScript packages) with a Python `crib_worker` subprocess for offline multimodal extraction. This is a DRAFT skeleton bible authored before per-symbol/file/cluster analyses exist — it will be superseded by the full system pass.
responsibilities: Parse source code into symbol + edge facts across TS/JS, Python, Rust, Go, Java, C#, PHP, PL/SQL (packages/parsers)
Resolve and link symbols across files into a sharded persistent soul graph (packages/pipeline)
Store/serve the soul graph, manifest, shards, dossiers (packages/core)
Expose deterministic query verbs + LLM enrichment work-queue over MCP (packages/mcp)
Provide the user-facing CLI: index, query, enrich, viz, export (packages/cli)
Define the soul schema: stable ids, Edge/Evidence/Manifest types, content hashing (packages/soul-schema)
Render the graph as an interactive viz (packages/ui)
Perform offline multimodal extraction via Python subprocess (python/crib_worker)
risks: parsers dominate symbol count (1367) and are heavily duplicated per-language (Parser.next/peek/isOp repeated across rust/csharp/go/java/python) — high maintenance surface
LLM layer at 0% coverage except 6 cli symbols — bible is currently ungrounded draft
Python crib_worker is a separate runtime; failures there degrade multimodal extraction silently
sideEffects: Spawns python crib_worker subprocess for multimodal extraction
whatToDistrust: DRAFT skeleton — not yet grounded in per-symbol/file/cluster analyses; will be superseded by the full system pass.
Module purposes are heuristic labels from the indexer ('controller/component/function/method module'), not authored semantics.
No per-symbol business rules yet — the 4 rules above are inferred from top symbols only.
Cross-cutting flows are hypothesized from module structure, not traced through actual call chains.
